title: Elevation Profile: Route Ascent, Descent, Grade
description: Build an elevation profile for any route with Elevation Profile — total ascent and descent, min and max height, steepest grade, chart included. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a 12.4 km ridge walk gaining 640 m of total ascent averages 51.6 m of climb per kilometre — the profile turns that one number into the whole story of where the climbing lives.
quick_answer: Elevation Profile charts the height of the ground along any route you click on the map, and totals it: minimum and maximum elevation, total ascent and descent, and the steepest grade. Draw the route and read its shape — the difference between a walk and a climb, made visible.

body.t: Total ascent — not summit height — is what legs feel. Profile the route before the boots commit; point heights come from the
Steepest grade decides gearing and honesty: a ride averaging 5.2% with one 14% wall is two different rides, and the profile names both.
Organisers publish profiles because runners plan pacing by them — where the climb sits (mile 2 or mile 20) changes the race.
A proposed access road's grade against vehicle and code limits starts as a profile across the terrain, before any surveyor is hired.

Total ascent (640 m) exceeds the start-to-finish height change on any rolling route — every dip re-buys its height. The profile's ascent figure is the honest one; the endpoints' difference is the liar.

A sustained 5.2% average (640 m over 12.4 km) is a solid mountain walk; roads for cars rarely sustain over 6–7%, and the steepest pitch on the profile — not the average — is where trailers and knees complain.

faq: Can I profile a route from a GPX file?

This page builds routes by clicking; GPX files from watches and apps carry their own recorded elevation, which their native apps profile best. Click the same line here when you want the terrain model's impartial version.
Why does my watch disagree with the profile?

Barometric watches measure air pressure live (accurate day to day, drifting with weather); the profile samples a stored terrain model. Differences of a few percent in total ascent are normal between the methods.
What is a good grade for a driveway?
Most vehicles and codes are comfortable under about 10–12% sustained; beyond that, ice and loaded trucks vote no. The profile's steepest-grade figure is the number to hold against local rules.
Does the profile include bridges and tunnels?
Terrain models mostly follow the ground surface — a route over a gorge bridge will profile the gorge unless the model's data says otherwise. Read cliff-edge artefacts with that in mind.
How long a route can I draw?
As long as patience allows clicks. Very long routes are better sketched in segments — the totals add, and each segment's shape stays legible.
Charts stretch the vertical axis so relief is visible; the numbers (ascent, grade) are computed from true values, not from the stretched picture.
Heights and distances show in both conventions — feet and miles for the US reader, metres and kilometres alongside.
